name: law_firm_software_002_privilege_clawback_audit
instruction: Audit the firm's finalised and served e-discovery productions for privileged material that left the firm, applying the firm's clawback procedure PRIV-CLAWBACK-01 (in firm_policies), batched under the episode batch code (ops_meta), as of the episode date. Which documents a production actually produced is derivable from the production's own Bates fields and each document's bates_number; the policy decides which of those disclosures are clawback violations -- including which productions are exempt, how the two privilege classifications differ, and what the log's reason must say about them. Log every violation the policy identifies as privilege_log rows (event='clawback_required', carrying the document's real ids and flagged with the episode date), then summarise what the log now contains: one ops_reports row per affected matter (report='clawback_followup') with that matter's violation count, its produced-document count, and the exposure ratio between them, plus one firm-wide summary row (report='privilege_clawback_audit') carrying the productions checked, the documents found inside production ranges, and the violations found. No other privilege_log or ops_reports rows for this batch_code under those two report names may exist. Do not modify ediscovery_documents or ediscovery_productions -- the produced record stays exactly as it is; the violation is logged externally, the way a real clawback notice would be. Every collection this task doesn't write to must remain untouched.

hazards.mechanism: 7 in-range privileged documents on uncovered finalised/served productions must each be logged with their privilege classification (planted: 6 bulk + the hand-authored DEF000001 on PROD-2026-001; snapshot-confirmed: 7). Missing any is an unlogged clawback exposure.

4 in-range privileged documents sit on productions with clawback_order_status='covered' (planted, snapshot-confirmed: 4) -- PRIV-CLAWBACK-01 says a 502(d)-style order means inadvertent disclosure does not waive privilege; flagging any of them = FAIL.

37 draft productions exist in the current snapshot (snapshot-confirmed) and PRIV-CLAWBACK-01 excludes them from clawback exposure; logging any document whose only range match is a draft production = FAIL.

338 filler documents carry privilege != 'none' but sit OUTSIDE every production Bates range (snapshot-confirmed: 338) -- a privilege-only scan with no range derivation over-reports by 338 plausible wrong log rows.

success_criteria.summary: One privilege_log row per genuine in-range privileged document on an uncovered finalised/served production (planted: 7, snapshot-confirmed), each carrying the document's real ids, the production's real id, and a reason that names the document's privilege classification; none for covered productions, draft productions, or out-of-range documents. One clawback_followup row per affected matter whose counts derive from the logged rows, and one privilege_clawback_audit summary row whose productions_checked/documents_in_range/violations_found match the live-computed set exactly. Both the in-range and violation counts are confirmed two independent ways (raw-row Bates filtering and a SQL join) which must agree. ediscovery_documents and ediscovery_productions untouched.

checks.expect: exactly the policy-derived violation set, classified per privilege type
in-range and violation counts agree between raw-row Bates filtering and a SQL join
per-matter followup rows derived from the written log rows; firm summary counts exact

checks.collection: all seeded collections outside blast_radius, including ediscovery_documents and ediscovery_productions

top_results: Clawback Agreements and FRE 502: A Practical Guide (americanbar.org)
Inadvertent Production of Privileged Documents: What to Do (reuters.com/legal)

uniqueness_searches.query: e-discovery bates range privilege audit benchmark task clawback agent
top_results: Bates Numbering and Document Production Standards (exterro.com)

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Distinct from generic 'find privileged documents' tasks: production membership is derived from a numeric Bates range rather than a stored link, the covered/none 502(d) distinction and the attorney_client vs work_product classification come from the seeded policy (not the instruction), and three near-miss classes (covered productions, draft productions, out-of-range privileged filler) each fail a naive solution in a different way.
